A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same APPLE study, with complete text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H. Full text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the version stamp and acknowledgments page.

before.justification: v4.pdf reports original classification, volume-estimation, and pose-estimation experiments in Section 4, plus ablations and additional experimental results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v5.pdf retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix C, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and CIFAR-10 evaluation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same APPLE-SAC and APPLE-CrossQ procedures, shared transformer architecture, prediction objectives, reward recomputation, and policy updates.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MHSB, CircleSquare, TactileMNIST classification and volume estimation, Toolbox, and CIFAR-10. The sparse-reward and CircleSquareHideAndSeek scenarios in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is identical in corresponding experiments, including APPLE-RND and HAM, and the appendix comparisons involving PPO, LSTM, pure-RL, grid-search, and NO-PRED variants.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C and E retain identical evaluation metrics, held-out evaluation settings, preprocessing, episode lengths, training budgets, and hyperparameter-search procedures.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same architecture and supervision ablations, grid-search comparison, sparse-reward test, downstream-task analysis, and longer HAM evaluations. Learned-policy visualizations in Figures 8 and 12 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same run-count disclosures, including five-seed evaluations and single-seed hyperparameter trials. Standard-deviation shading and its descriptions in Figures 4 and 21 are identical.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, learning curves, rankings, and qualitative findings are identical, including Figures 4–6 and 14–21. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The POMDP definitions, assumptions, objectives, and gradient decomposition in Section 3 are unchanged. The appendix loss definitions and detailed derivation in Appendix G are also identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about APPLE's unified formulation, SAC/CrossQ variants, and applicability across classification and regression without task-specific exploration heuristics.

C2.justification: Interpretations of exploration behavior, sample reuse, and CrossQ robustness are unchanged. Sections 5–6 and Appendix D retain the same limitations concerning sample efficiency, real-world deployment, and broader sensing configurations.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement, code-access information, Table 1 hyperparameters, and implementation, hardware, memory, and runtime details in Appendices E–F are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with HAM and the discussion of curiosity-based intrinsic rewards in Appendix H.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments on page 11 add Chiron, Astérix, and PSPC FAIR WASTE funding credits and revise the surrounding sentence. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; scientific prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgments slightly reflow subsequent text and reference spacing on page 11. Figures 1–21, Table 1, equation displays, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5.pdf adds funding acknowledgments and updates the version stamp, with minor local reflow. Scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, so these administrative edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
